proposals.before: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, came from Fenyin in Tongzhou and claimed Tang’s Prince of Pingyang, Hui, as ancestor.
proposals.after: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, came from Fengyi in Tongzhou and claimed Tang’s Prince of Pingyang, Hui, as ancestor.
proposals.reason: 馮翊 is Fengyi (Tongzhou seat), not Fenyin; place-name error in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, was a native of Fenyin in Tongzhou; he claimed descent from Tang’s Prince of Pingyang, Hui.
proposals.after: Jing Xiang, styled Zizhen, was a native of Fengyi in Tongzhou; he claimed descent from Tang’s Prince of Pingyang, Hui.
proposals.reason: 馮翊 should be Fengyi, not Fenyin, in the literal English as well.

proposals.before: The army set out toward Guangzhou, was stopped by torrential rain, then besieged Shouzhou without success and lost heavily; only then did Taizu bitterly repent.
proposals.after: The army set out toward Guang Prefecture (Guangzhou), was stopped by torrential rain, then besieged Shouzhou without success and lost heavily; only then did Taizu bitterly repent.
proposals.reason: 光州 is Guang Prefecture in Huainan circuit, easily confused with 廣州; mark the prefecture clearly.

proposals.before: As a commander Zhen excelled at discipline and choosing men; when Taizu first held Xuanyi, Zhen built his army system, picking officers and drilling troops with real art.
proposals.after: As a commander Zhen excelled at discipline and choosing men; when Taizu first held Xuanwu, Zhen built his army system, picking officers and drilling troops with real art.
proposals.reason: 宣武 is the Xuanwu governorship; Xuanyi is a misspelling/mistranslation.

proposals.before: When Taizu of Liang held Xuannu, he raised five hundred horses into a cavalry force and gave Shigu command; under him Shigu helped break Huang Chao and Qin Zongquan.
proposals.after: When Taizu of Liang held Xuanwu, he raised five hundred horses into a cavalry force and gave Shigu command; under him Shigu helped break Huang Chao and Qin Zongquan.
proposals.reason: 宣武 should be Xuanwu, not Xuannu.

proposals.before: At Luzhou Feng Ba killed the Jin commander Li Keqin and surrendered to Liang. Taizu sent Congzhou in; Jin attacked; Congzhou could not hold and fled to Heyang.
proposals.after: At Luzhou Feng Ba killed the Jin commander Li Kegong and surrendered to Liang. Taizu sent Congzhou in; Jin attacked; Congzhou could not hold and fled to Heyang.
proposals.reason: 李克恭 is Li Kegong; Keqin is a different Li (克勤/克用 family naming confusion).

proposals.before: Ge Congzhou, styled Tongmei, came from Zhencheng in Puzhou.
proposals.after: Ge Congzhou, styled Tongmei, came from Juancheng in Puzhou.
proposals.reason: 濮州甄城 is conventionally Juancheng; Zhencheng is a nonstandard reading.

proposals.before: Taizu made Congzhou campaign marshal of Xuanyi.
proposals.after: Taizu made Congzhou campaign marshal of Xuanwu.
proposals.reason: 宣義/宣武 naming: packet has Xuanyi; prefer Xuanwu/Xuanyi consistency for 宣義.

proposals.before: When Taizu first secured Xuannwu, he made Han a guest officer and sent him with Zhu Zhen to raise troops in Ziqing.
proposals.after: When Taizu first secured Xuanwu, he made Han a guest officer and sent him with Zhu Zhen to raise troops in Ziqing.
proposals.reason: 宣武 is Xuanwu, not Xuannwu.

proposals.before: His family had served the Xuannwu Army as staff officers for generations.
proposals.after: His family had served the Xuanwu Army as staff officers for generations.
proposals.reason: 宣武 is Xuanwu, not Xuannwu.
